cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values: range = maximum – minimum; it is affected by outliers.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: The interquartile range (IQR) = Q3 – Q1; it measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data and is not affected by outliers.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: The IQR is preferred over the range when the data contains outliers or is skewed, because it ignores extreme values.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: The pth percentile is the value below which p% of the data falls; it can be read from a cumulative frequency curve.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: The 10th percentile (P10) is the value at 10% of the total cumulative frequency; the 90th percentile (P90) is at 90%.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: The interpercentile range is the difference between two percentiles, e.g. P90 – P10, which captures the middle 80% of the data.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: The interpercentile range is more stable than the range because it excludes extreme values, similar to how the IQR works.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: Variance measures the average squared deviation from the mean: σ² = Σ(x – x̄)² ÷ n (population) or s² = Σ(x – x̄)² ÷ (n – 1) (sample).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: Standard deviation (SD) is the square root of the variance; it measures spread in the same units as the original data.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: A larger standard deviation means the data is more spread out from the mean; a smaller SD means the data is closer to the mean.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: For grouped data, the estimated standard deviation uses midpoints: s = √[Σf(x – x̄)² ÷ (Σf – 1)] where x is the midpoint of each class.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Spread
cards.back: When comparing two distributions, compare both a measure of central tendency (e.g. median) and a measure of spread (e.g. IQR or SD).
